name: Samoosas
summary: Crisp pastry triangles packed with dry-spiced beef mince, onion and fresh coriander, fried golden: the Cape and Durban favourite for Eid, Diwali and every tea table.
about: South Africa spells it samoosa. Brought by Cape Malay and Indian South African cooks, the fried triangles are a fixture of iftar tables during Ramadan, of Eid and Diwali visits and of corner-shop counters in Cape Town and Durban. Families often make them in big batches together and freeze them, ready to fry when guests arrive.

ingredients.name: Samoosa pastry strips
ingredients.note: pur pastry, thawed and kept under a damp cloth

steps: Mix the onion with ½ tsp of the salt and leave for 5 minutes. Squeeze it hard in a clean tea towel to remove as much liquid as you can, so the filling stays dry.

Put the mince in a large dry frying pan over medium-high heat with the ginger and garlic paste, turmeric, chilli powder, ground coriander, cumin and the remaining salt. Cook for 15–20 minutes, breaking it up finely with a wooden spoon, until all the liquid has cooked away and the mince is crumbly and dry.

Take the pan off the heat and stir in the garam masala. Spread the mince on a tray and cool completely, about 20 minutes. Only then stir in the squeezed onion, green chillies, fresh coriander and spring onions (warm mince wilts them and makes the pastry soggy).
Mix the flour and water into a thick, smooth paste for sealing.

Hold a pastry strip vertically. Fold the bottom corner across to make a triangle, then fold that triangle up once more to form a cone. Fill the cone with a heaped tablespoon of mince, pressing it in gently.

Keep folding the triangle up along the strip until you reach the end. Brush the last flap with flour paste and press it closed, making sure the corners are sealed. Lay the finished samoosas under a damp cloth while you fold the rest.
Heat the oil in a deep pot over medium heat to 170 °C, or until a scrap of pastry sizzles and floats straight away. Never leave hot oil unattended.
Fry 6–8 samoosas at a time for 3–4 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden all over. Drain on paper towel and serve warm with lemon wedges.
prepNote: Makes about 30. Freeze folded, unfried samoosas on a tray, then bag; fry from frozen in oil that is not yet fully hot.
